title: PUT /api/content writes after the antivirus scan with the rights that existed before the scan
description: The route evaluates need(write), the quota user and ownerOfPath before the awaited antivirus gate, and does not re-check them after it. A user whose write permission is removed while the scan runs still has the in-flight save written, while a fresh PUT is refused with 403. Reproduced for the permission downgrade; the delete/recreate variant is reported by the hunter only.
root_cause: need() at line 215, quotaUserOf at 216 and ownerOfPath at 220 are computed before await gate() at 233; nothing between the gate and writeFileAtomic at 255 calls need() again or compares the account instance.
intended_behavior: Re-run need(..., 'write') and the account-instance check after the scan, in the same tick as the quota hold, and compute owner after the scan.

trace.description: need(user, space, 'write') evaluated once at request start
await gate() can take up to the antivirus timeout, no re-authorization afterwards
writeFileAtomic(abs, body.content) with the pre-scan authorization

evidence.description: After the scan only ready(q), ready(owner) and a stat are done; no permission or account check. Local run with a 1.5 s fake clamd: permissions set to ['read'] mid-scan, the in-flight PUT returned 200 and the file was overwritten, a fresh PUT returned 403 (two runs).

conditions.description: Antivirus enabled (off by default) so the scan opens a window
Rights removed while the scan of an already authorized request runs (seconds)

execution.attacker_perspective: user whose write right is being removed
instructions: Enable antivirus against a fake clamd delaying 1.5 s
After 400 ms an admin sets bob's permissions to ['read']
A fresh PUT gives 403; the in-flight one returns 200 and the file holds the new text

remediation.strategy: After the scan call need() again and compare the account instance, then compute owner and hold in the same tick.

likelihood.reason: needs antivirus on and a rights change inside a seconds-long scan window

impact.reason: one text edit up to MAX_TEXT by a principal whose rights were just removed

confidence.reason: permission variant reproduced twice in the sandbox; delete/recreate variant from hunter artifacts only

title: A pending timer write of the running app overwrites a CLI sessions-revoke and restores revoked app passwords / sessions
description: bun src/cli.ts sessions-revoke (and reset-2fa) edits sessions.json and app-passwords.json and then touches cli-changed; the running app re-reads them only at the start of the next request. If an app write fires first (app-password lastUsedAt timer after 5 s, hourly purgeExpiredSessions), it writes the old in-memory data over the CLI's files and the next request reloads that file, so the revoked app password or session works again. The CLI still reports success.
root_cause: JsonStore.writeNow/persist write the in-memory snapshot without checking whether the cli-changed marker moved; the marker is checked only in request hooks (context.ts, webdav.ts handleDav).
intended_behavior: Operator revocation is final: the running app must not keep honouring or write back old sessions or app passwords (comment in app-passwords.ts:105-106).

trace.description: destroyUserSessions and removeAppPasswordsOf write the files in the CLI process; the marker is touched at line 101
updateSoon leaves a 5 s timer whose snapshot comes from the app's old in-memory list
serialises this.data over the file with no marker or mtime check
the next request reloads the already overwritten files, so the revocation is lost

evidence.description: writeNow persists the stale snapshot without checking the CLI marker
purgeExpiredSessions uses sessionStore.update, which writes the whole in-memory sessions map (hourly, index.ts:122)
onCliChange reload happens only inside a request, so a timer can fire first

conditions.description: Operator runs the CLI on the host; the beneficiary holds the revoked app password or session cookie
A timer write (5 s app-password lastUsedAt, or hourly purge) must fire after the CLI write and before any request reaches the app; a request in between reloads and heals

execution.attacker_perspective: Holder of a revoked WebDAV app password or session cookie after the operator ran sessions-revoke
payloads: PROPFIND /dav/ with Authorization: Basic alice:<app password>
instructions: Start the app on a scratch DATA_DIR, create alice with an app password and carol with a session
PROPFIND once with the app password (queues the 5 s timer)
Run the CLI sessions-revoke alice on the same DATA_DIR
Send no request for 6.5 s, then PROPFIND with the old secret
execution.observed_result: Reproduced twice in the sandbox: app-passwords.json 0 items after the CLI, 1 after the timer, PROPFIND 207 with the revoked secret. Control (request right after the CLI): 401, disk 0. Session variant: after purgeExpiredSessions() GET /api/session returns carol.

remediation.strategy: Check the cli-changed marker (reload first) inside writeNow/persist before serialising, or have the app watch the marker on a short interval and drop pending timers; add a regression test running the CLI while a touchAppPassword timer is pending.

likelihood.reason: Needs a pending timer or the hourly tick to land in the gap before the next request

impact.reason: Operator emergency revocation of a stolen credential is silently undone while the CLI reports success

confidence.reason: Independently reproduced twice in the sandbox with a passing control

title: WebDAV PUT completes with the credential and rights it had when the request started, after the app password was revoked
description: authenticate() verifies the app password once; putMethod then resolves the Space, permissions and quota user once and, after the unbounded body loop and gate(), re-checks only ready(), ownerOfPath, preconditions and holdNow before place(). Revoking the app password while the body streams does not stop the write: a new PROPFIND gets 401 but the running PUT gets 201 and the file is written. Deleted/re-created accounts and lowered rights are expected to behave the same by source (perms copied at start, quota keyed by username) but were not re-run by this verifier.
root_cause: putMethod never re-verifies the app password record, the account instance (name, createdAt) or accessFor perms between the start of the request and place(); the body can stream for an unbounded time and quota commit is keyed by lowercase username.
intended_behavior: Revoking an app password, deleting the account or lowering its rights must stop a PUT that has not yet been placed: re-check the app password item, the account instance and upload/write perms right before holdNow/place and fail with 401/403.

trace.description: app password verified once; user and item captured in ctx
allow(s,'upload') on the Space resolved at request start
body loop with no total deadline and no re-auth
place(tmp, s.abs, written) writes the file with the stale authority

evidence.description: Verifier run twice in sandbox: app password revoked mid-body, PROPFIND 401, PUT 201 and file content helloworld written (exit 42 both runs)
commitBytes keys the counter by username, not account instance

conditions.description: holder of a valid app password at request start
revocation happens while the body is still streaming or the scan is running; the client controls the pace

execution.attacker_perspective: Holder of a WebDAV app password that is revoked while their upload is open
payloads: PUT /dav/home/f.txt with a slow ReadableStream body: send 5 bytes, revoke the app password, send 5 more bytes
instructions: Create user with readwrite app password
Start PUT with a ReadableStream body and send 5 of 10 bytes
DELETE /api/me/app-passwords/<id>; PROPFIND with it now returns 401
Send the remaining bytes and close
execution.observed_result: PROPFIND after revoke 401; PUT 201; file f.txt contains helloworld (two runs).

remediation.strategy: Before holdNow/place re-verify the app password item still exists and is unexpired, the account instance is the same, and accessFor still grants upload (and write when replacing); bound total PUT duration; key quota by account instance.

likelihood.reason: needs a valid credential and a revocation timed during an open upload

impact.reason: one in-flight file within the upload limit is written after revocation; no other-user data read or changed demonstrated

confidence.reason: revocation variant reproduced twice; other variants follow from source
